contribution_claim: We show that the initial active ratio rho0 in ternary pre-training is locked near 0.69 for every zero-mean initialiser, independently of sigma, and make it tunable. In a pre-registered comparison over 1.4M-352M parameters with 8 arms and 15 seeds we find that MOVING THE INITIAL OPERATING POINT DEGRADES QUALITY, while approaching the same point GRADUALLY over training improves it consistently. A mechanism-matched control (TWN-style constant threshold scaling) beats the init-distribution variant at every scale, locating the effect in the TIMING of the threshold rather than in the initial weight distribution.

claim_frozen_at.when: main grid at dim640; ~90 GPU-hours remaining
claim_frozen_at.evidence_basis: LR calibration (88/88 cells) + completed confirmatory cells dim192-dim512, seed means only
claim_frozen_at.note: No Cell 13 hypothesis test had been run when this was written.

claim_prior_art: TTQ (Zhu et al. ICLR 2017) = fixed sparsity ratio as a hyperparameter
Hyperspherical LATQ (Liu et al. 2022) = gradual threshold, CNN regime
Sparse TNN (2017) = threshold as an explicit sparsity control

scale_model.note: primary estimator regresses on scale MEANS because H6 asks about variation across scales and the unit of that question is the scale; seed-clustered intervals are anticonservative here (see R43)

efficiency.caveat: measured numbers are the cost of SIMULATING ternary in bf16 (STE keeps bf16 master weights and adds quant/norm work); they are NOT ternary inference numbers and must not be read as such. No ternary kernel was benchmarked in this work.

plateau_gate_definition: slope test with 95% CI on held-out val trace over the last plateau_frac of probes; rejects descending (undertrained) and ascending (unstable) tails; requires >= plateau_min_tail probes

revisions.R20_shadowed_lsuv_definitions: cell 8 defined init_xavier/init_kaiming/init_lsuv and lsuv_calibrate TWICE; python keeps the LAST binding, so the version that ran was the older pre-R13 one -- R13 was silently undone inside its own cell. Consequences: (a) LSUV_DEGENERATE was NEVER written (all three assignments live in the first definition), so this manifest field reported nulls under prose claiming the value was measured, and the LSUV-is-degenerate finding was unmeasurable; (b) the preflight check 'LSUV_DEGENERATE.is_noop == true' could never pass; (c) tol reverted 0.01 -> 0.10, exactly the loosening R13 documented tightening. Duplicate block removed. Found by grepping for duplicate top-level definitions -- invisible to linear reading.
revisions.R25_compile_enabled_on_measurement: torch.compile turned ON after direct measurement on the target A100, not on expectation: 2.03x at dim512, 1.71x at dim384, with an eager-vs-compiled val_loss delta of 0.051 against a same-code run-to-run noise floor of 0.029 -- the first benchmark had flagged 0.058 as disqualifying, but that comparison HAD NO CONTROL, and flash attention is already non-deterministic. Measuring the noise floor reversed the decision. Compile also lowered peak VRAM 10.09 -> 8.88 GB. The preflight A/B re-verifies on the real corpus before the grid starts. Also tested and REJECTED: casting normalisation weights to fp32 to recover the fused rms_norm kernel (the profile showed aten::copy_ at 16% of CUDA time and a dtype-mismatch warning every step). It was SLOWER -- 0.88x eager, 0.97x compiled, and +1.7 GB -- because the extra fp32<->bf16 conversions cost more than the unfused kernel. Under compile the issue is moot: inductor fuses the norm regardless. Hypothesis tested, disproved, not applied.
revisions.R27_embedding_never_initialised: Found in Phase 0. nn.Embedding defaults to normal_(0,1) and is TIED to the output head, so initial logits had std ~ sqrt(dim) and the loss at step 0 was 121.6 / 211.4 / 351.9 at dim192 / dim384 / dim768, against a uniform-prediction baseline of log(50257)=10.83. apply_init walks BitLinear layers only; nothing ever touched the embedding, so all eight arms inherited the PyTorch default. This initially looked like divergence -- losses of 50-120 that grew with model size -- but it was the STARTING point, not a blow-up: every run was descending correctly from an absurd origin, and the apparent scaling with model size was just sqrt(dim). Why it matters here more than in an ordinary training script: (a) a large slice of the FIXED 20M token budget goes to shrinking the embedding norm before any language modelling starts, and that budget was chosen to reach a plateau; (b) the waste grows as sqrt(dim), biasing H6 and the scaling-law fit in a direction unrelated to rho0; (c) this is a paper about INITIALISATION, and a large init-driven transient common to all arms dilutes the effect under test -- it could mask a real TAI advantage as easily as fabricate one. Set to the standard GPT-2 std=0.02, giving initial loss 10.88/10.92/11.00 -- at the baseline and, importantly, scale-independent. A bug fix rather than a tuning choice: the prior state was 'uninitialised'. Identical across arms and touches no BitLinear, so the ternary mechanism under test is unaffected.
revisions.R37_h3_narrowed_to_retention: Recorded from the dim384 sweep BEFORE the dim768 sweep, the placebo arm, or any Cell 13 statistic had run, so the revised wording is not a description of a finished result. Sweeping rho0 from 0.40 to 0.70 changes INITIAL sparsity by thirty points (0.60 -> 0.30) and leaves TWO points at the end (0.3240 -> 0.3025). A linear fit gives final = 0.2800 + 0.0714 * initial with R^2 = 0.978: the retention coefficient is 0.071, so roughly 93% of the intervention is undone by training, and the implied fixed point 0.3015 is essentially where the `standard` arm lands unaided (~0.313). H3 AS PRE-REGISTERED -- that the initial operating point causally SHAPES final sparsity -- is therefore NOT supported in its strong form. What the data do support is narrower: a small, strictly ordered, extremely reliable residue (rho0 0.40 vs 0.70 gives +0.0216, p=8.5e-15, d=44.6, against a within-seed sparsity SD of 0.0004) sitting on top of an attractor near 0.30 that training reaches from wherever it starts. This reframes the paper rather than weakening it: the locked ~0.69 value is not merely a default every zero-mean initialiser happens to share, it is where the optimisation GOES -- which explains H1, since quality improves monotonically as rho0 moves back toward the locked point (5.2519 -> 5.1901), exactly why `tai` loses to `standard` while `tai_warmup`, which approaches the same point gradually, wins. This is a REPORTING change, not an analysis change: the sweep, the placebo arm and every test are untouched, and retention is computed for every swept (scale, arm) including tai_negctrl, whose retention slope remains the falsification instrument -- a placebo slope comparable to the real one would mean even the narrowed effect is artefact.
revisions.R44_manifest_depended_on_a_helper_from_a: R42's json_safe() lives in Cell 10 with the run store, and Cell 15 called it by name. That works in a linear Run All and fails the moment a cell is skipped, re-ordered, or the analysis is re-run in a fresh kernel from the run store -- which is the normal way to regenerate artifacts without a GPU. The manifest is the last output of a multi-day experiment; losing it to a missing four-line helper is a failure mode worth removing outright, so Cell 15 now falls back to a local definition. Found by the offline dry-run harness, not by a session.
revisions.R45_h2_companion_token_equal_test: The pre-registered H2 is an equivalence claim about CONVERGED quality, tested by TOST over plateau-verified paired seeds. With 0 of 760 runs reaching plateau it was skipped at every scale, so H2 -- one of the four primary hypotheses -- went entirely unreported. The pre-registered verdict remains UNTESTABLE and is printed and stored as such; it is not overwritten. Alongside it we now run a clearly labelled COMPANION test of the weaker claim the data supports: equivalence at a fixed 20M-token budget over all paired seeds. Three reasons this is not a post-hoc rescue. (1) The re-statement is forced by a measurement -- the budget does not reach plateau, confirmed independently by the 2x-budget check -- not by an outcome. (2) It does not favour the method: it rejects equivalence for BOTH arms, reporting tai as WORSE and tai_warmup as BETTER by roughly ten to thirty times the margin at every scale. A substitution that makes the eponymous arm fail is not the shape p-hacking takes. (3) Both results go into the manifest under separate keys (h2_prereg_status, h2_token_equal_companion), so which test was pre-registered and which was added is never in doubt.
revisions.R46_offline_dryrun_harness: Process change, prompted by six consecutive crashes (R38-R43) in the analysis chain, each costing a Colab session to discover. The common cause was structural: those code paths only become reachable once the full grid exists, so no smoke test could reach them. Now that the run store is complete, dryrun.py executes cells 12 through 16 against the REAL 3016-run store on CPU in seconds, with the GPU, Drive and network layers stubbed and the cell source otherwise unmodified. It immediately found R44 and would have caught R38-R43. Every future edit to the analysis chain is validated end-to-end before it reaches a GPU session.
revisions.R43_h6_slope_singular_and_the_obvious_re: The pre-registered H6 estimator, mixedlm(eff ~ logp, groups=seed), failed on the completed grid with 'Random effects covariance is singular' and fell through to a descriptive OLS that printed a slope WITH NO INTERVAL. A point estimate without uncertainty is not a result, so H6 was in effect unreported. Cause: the seed-level random intercept has almost nothing to estimate -- between-seed SD of the effect is 0.017 against a between-scale SD of 0.046 -- so the covariance collapses to the boundary. The tempting repair, OLS with SEs clustered on seed, is worse than the failure because it answers the wrong question: H6 asks whether the effect varies WITH SCALE, and the unit of that question is the scale, of which there are 11. Clustering on seed treats the scales as independent replicates of one line and ignores scale-level residual structure, which here is as large as the seed noise (scale-level residual SD 0.042 vs within-scale seed SD 0.030). The consequence is not cosmetic -- all three estimators return the SAME slope (-0.0126) and opposite conclusions: clustered on seed CI [-0.0181,-0.0071] excludes zero, clustered on scale [-0.0236,-0.0016] excludes zero, and regression on the 11 scale means [-0.0291,+0.0037] SPANS zero. Picking the narrowest interval would manufacture a scale-dependence finding out of an analysis choice. The conservative scale-level regression is therefore PRIMARY, the other two are reported beside it as sensitivity analyses, all of them go into the manifest, and the code prints an explicit warning when they disagree about whether the CI covers zero. Operative reading for the paper: the direction of the tai_warmup effect is consistent across all 11 scales (that is the PRIMARY H6 sign test, which is unaffected), but the magnitude is NOT resolved as scale-varying.
revisions.R42_manifest_could_not_serialise_tuple_k: The manifest write -- the LAST artifact produced, after the entire compute budget has been spent -- died with "keys must be str, int, float, bool or None, not tuple". LRSTAR and LR_CURVE, added to the manifest by R33, are keyed by the tuple (size, method), and json.dumps rejects non-scalar KEYS outright; the `default=str` fallback already in place does not help, because it is consulted for unknown VALUES only. Every phase had completed and the provenance record for the whole experiment was discarded at the final line. Fixed at source (both fields flattened to 'size/method') and, because auditing forty-odd manifest fields by hand is a check that rots the moment someone adds a dict, with a shared json_safe() helper that recursively normalises keys, applied to the manifest and to the efficiency dump. A second failure surfaced while testing the first: json.dumps(sort_keys=True), needed for a stable hash, cannot order a dict mixing int and str keys either -- so keys are coerced to STRINGS rather than merely to json-legal types, which makes the ordering total and the hash reproducible. Verified against the real run store: 88 tuple-keyed calibration cells serialise cleanly and hash stably.
revisions.R41_module_level_names_shadowed_import_a: Cell 12 assigned the count of architecture-x-scale cells to the name `nn`, which is the module-level alias for torch.nn established in Cell 5. Notebook cells share ONE namespace, so from that line on torch.nn WAS AN INTEGER, and the next phase to construct a model -- the width-control ladder -- died inside LM.__init__ with "'int' object has no attribute 'Embedding'". The traceback pointed at the model, hundreds of lines from the cause, and the same crash would have hit the cross-architecture and ablation phases. An AST scan of all 60 import aliases found two more of the same kind: `_t` (the `import time as _t` alias) was rebound both by the quantiser self-test in Cell 5 and by a t-statistic in Cell 12, and `_m` (`import math as _m`) was rebound by a demo model in Cell 8. None had surfaced because the colliding cells happened to run before the alias was first needed -- pure luck of ordering, not correctness. All four renamed (_n_cells, _tq, _tstat, _mdl), and the check is now permanent: verify_patch.py fails if any module-level assignment or for-target rebinds an import alias anywhere in the notebook.
revisions.R40_statistics_iterated_over_unrun_scale: The primary statistics cell looped over SIZES, the full 12-point ladder, rather than over the scales that were actually run. SIZES includes dim2048 (783M), which is opt-in and absent from SCALES_TO_RUN, so for that scale rows was empty, the per-method summary stayed empty, and the primary-baseline fallback called min() on an empty sequence: ValueError, raised AFTER all eleven completed scales had already been analysed and printed, discarding the entire cell's work. The loop now runs over scales with at least one record and announces the skip instead of passing over it silently, and the fallback itself guards against an empty candidate set so a baseline can never be chosen from nothing. Verified against the real store with dim2048 present in SIZES: eleven scales analysed, one skipped, no exception. This is the third failure in the same family as R38 and R39 -- code paths that only execute once the full grid exists, and therefore could not be reached until the grid finished.
revisions.R39_diverged_runs_declared_only_on_the_d: DIVERGED_RUNS was initialised on a line that lives inside the ARM_FULL_RUN=False branch -- the safe-mode path where nothing trains. On any real run the name never came into existence, so R26's collector and R38's invariant assert both referenced an undefined global and the cell died with NameError AFTER the whole run store had been reloaded. The bug was latent from R26 and only surfaced when R38's assert reached the name on a path R26's own branch never took. All three accumulators are now declared unconditionally at module level, guarded so that re-running the cell inside a live session does not wipe a list an earlier pass filled. Second defect fixed in the same place: the collection loop reset RESULTS but not DIVERGED_RUNS or PLATEAU_STATS, so a second pass over the store in one session would append duplicates and trip R38's invariant with a confusing off-by-N. All three now reset together. Verified end-to-end against the real store on a fresh namespace: 760 records collected, assert passes, and a second pass leaves the count unchanged.
revisions.R38_results_collection_lost_99_percent_o: A one-level indentation error, introduced by the R26 divergence filter, put the collection block in the `method` loop instead of the `seed` loop. After the seed loop finished, only the LAST seed's record was examined, so exactly ONE run per (scale, method) entered RESULTS instead of all 5 or 15. Verified against the real store: 760 completed runs would have yielded 88 records. Every confirmatory test consumes RESULTS, so H1/H2/H4 would have been computed at n=1 per cell -- paired tests would have collapsed or thrown, and any number that survived would have been meaningless. Entirely silent: 88 is a plausible-looking count and nothing asserted the expected size. Fixed, and an assert now checks the invariant len(RESULTS)+len(DIVERGED_RUNS)==sum over scales of methods*seeds, so a future edit that breaks the collection fails loudly instead of quietly producing statistics over a hundredth of the data. This is the same failure mode as R15 and R16 -- code that runs, produces plausible output, and is wrong -- and it was introduced by a fix, not by the original design, which is exactly why the invariant is now asserted rather than trusted.
revisions.R37_h3_tested_the_wrong_sign_and_the_wro: Two problems, found when the first rho0 sweep cells completed and BEFORE the second sweep scale had run. (1) WRONG SIGN. rho0 is the initial ACTIVE ratio, so a higher rho0 means FEWER zeros and therefore LOWER sparsity: the relationship is necessarily decreasing. The pre-registered code tested whether the per-seed Spearman was centered ABOVE zero and counted seeds that were monotone NON-DECREASING in rho0 -- both the opposite expectation. Measured on dim384: per-seed Spearman is -1.000 on all 15 seeds and the old monotonicity counter reads 0.00. This was not benign: the old one-sample t-test returns t=-inf, p=0.0, so a reader scanning for a small p-value would have recorded H3 as strongly SUPPORTED while the monotonicity number beside it said 0.00 -- two headline figures in direct contradiction, with the significant-looking one pointing the wrong way. The test now checks the mechanism's actual prediction and states the expected direction in the printed output. (2) WRONG QUANTITY. A Spearman of -1 says the ORDER is preserved and nothing about MAGNITUDE, which is the entire claim. On dim384 a 30-point swing in initial sparsity (rho0 0.4->0.7, i.e. 0.60->0.30) leaves a 2.15-point spread in final sparsity (0.3240->0.3025): roughly 7% of the intervention survives, and all four operating points collapse toward ~0.31 -- the same value the `standard` arm reaches unaided. So the locked point is not merely a default, it is an ATTRACTOR. H3 is therefore NOT supported in its strong pre-registered form. A retention fraction (final swing / initial swing) is now computed as a first-class number, printed, and stored in the manifest as h3_retention, with h3_operative_wording derived from it so the paper cannot lean on the correlation alone. The fig5 title, which asserted 'initial operating point causally shapes final sparsity', now describes what is plotted and reports the retention instead of pre-judging it. Note this also explains H1: quality improves monotonically as rho0 approaches the locked value, which is why the tai arm loses to standard -- moving away from the attractor costs quality, and that is the coherent reading of all three results together.
revisions.R36_contribution_claim_frozen_mid_run: The contribution claim was rewritten and FROZEN while the main grid was at dim640, with ~90 GPU-hours still to run and not a single Cell 13 statistic computed. Recorded here, dated, for the same reason the hypotheses were pre-registered: a claim written after seeing every number is unfalsifiable and a reviewer cannot tell the difference. It CHANGED from the pre-registered framing, which expected TAI to win. Across five scales, at each arm's own optimal LR, the completed cells give tai - gamma_offset = +0.02..+0.15 (TAI worse, gap growing with scale), tai - standard = +0.06..+0.13 (TAI worse), and tai_warmup - standard = -0.13..-0.17 (warmup better, stable). The effect is real but it is not the hypothesised effect: the gain comes from moving the threshold gradually, not from where the operating point starts. The mechanism-matched control settles the attribution, since gamma_offset reaches the same operating point by threshold scaling and beats the init-distribution route at every scale -- so the active ingredient is the SCHEDULE, not the initial weight distribution. The claim is phrased to survive either direction of the remaining evidence; what would falsify it is the warmup gap crossing zero or gamma_offset losing to tai, and both remain possible. Prior art is named in claim_prior_art rather than left for a reviewer to find: gamma_offset is TWN (Li & Liu 2016) and is called that in the paper, gradual threshold increase is Hyperspherical LATQ (Liu et al. 2022) in the CNN setting, and Ternary Mamba (arXiv 2606.18114, June 2026) independently reports that a single asymmetric threshold moved sparsity 25.7% -> 20.9% at a cost of +0.12 PPL -- the same direction as our tai result in a different architecture and regime, cited as confirmation rather than competition. What is new is the three-way separation -- move the operating point at init, by threshold, or on a schedule -- in from-scratch LLM pre-training, with a placebo arm and 15 seeds.
revisions.R35_h2_wording_token_equal_not_converged: Recorded mid-run, from measurement, BEFORE any hypothesis test was computed. The pre-registration describes 20M tokens as a 'plateau-verified budget' and phrases H2 in terms of converged quality. The first 502 main-grid runs returned plateau_ok on ZERO of them: at dim384 the validation trace still falls ~0.21 nats across the final 40% of probes, and the picture is uniform across scales (-0.20 to -0.27). The plateau gate is not broken -- it is correctly reporting that the models are still learning when the budget ends. Nothing about the comparison is invalidated: a token-equal comparison at a fixed budget is a legitimate protocol and every arm is treated identically. What is invalidated is the WORDING. Every claim must read 'at a fixed 20M-token budget'; none may say 'at convergence' or 'converged quality'. H2's TOST is defined over plateau-verified pairs and is therefore reported as SKIPPED rather than computed over an empty set -- the statistics cell already guards n<2, so this is a reporting change, not a code change. The budget itself is deliberately NOT moved: it is pre-registered, and extending it now to manufacture a plateau would be precisely the post-hoc adjustment this harness exists to prevent. Cell 11c's 2x-budget check remains the pre-registered instrument for asking whether the ranking is budget-dependent. Added: a PLATEAU_STATS counter that makes the situation visible in the log and in the manifest (plateau_status, h2_operative_wording) rather than leaving it to be discovered by reading 500 run files.
revisions.R33_lr_grid_widened_and_adaptive: Session-1 calibration found the optimum ON A GRID BOUNDARY in 23 of the 32 confirmatory (scale, method) cells: every arm at dim256 and dim384 chose the top point 3e-3 with the curve still descending, and every arm at dim1280/dim1536 chose the bottom point 1e-3. A boundary optimum alone would be a tolerable limitation; what is not is that the boundary SLOPES differ by arm. At dim384 the 2e-3 to 3e-3 gain is +0.026 for gamma_offset and +0.046 for tai, a 1.8x difference, and the sign of that asymmetry flips at dim256. Since gamma_offset is the mechanism-matched control that decides whether TAI's contribution is the initialisation distribution or merely threshold control, a ranking sensitive to where the grid happened to stop would put the paper's central claim on an artifact -- and no post-hoc argument recovers it. Grid widened at both ends to [5e-4, 1e-3, 2e-3, 3e-3, 5e-3], plus adaptive extension: an argmin on an end point triggers one probe further out (x2 or /2), up to twice, so 'the optimum lies outside the grid' becomes a measured fact rather than an untestable caveat. Each summary record now stores lr_interior and the full probed grid, so any cell still pinned at a boundary is visible in the manifest instead of silent. Cost is modest because the run store keys on (scale, method, seed, lr): all 747 completed calibration runs are reused and only the new points are trained (~498 short runs). Stale LR* SUMMARY records are deleted automatically -- without that the cached three-point curve would short-circuit the whole change and the widening would silently do nothing. Also added: _validate_lr_proxy, which re-runs one calibration curve at FULL length at a single scale and seed and compares argmin and Spearman rank against the 300-step proxy. R22 chose 300 steps to save ~32% of compute, but with 120 warmup steps that is ~180 post-warmup steps of evidence applied to 1221-step runs, and high LRs flatter themselves early -- the same direction as the boundary problem, so the two confounds compound. The check is a few runs and converts an assumption into evidence the paper can cite; if it disagrees, lr_cal_steps must rise before the main grid is trusted.
revisions.R34_compile_only_for_long_runs: Session-1 timings showed torch.compile was a net LOSS on calibration runs. At dim1280 a 300-step run took 285 s: ~71 s training, ~28 s evaluation, ~190 s model construction plus compilation. The decisive evidence that compilation is paid PER RUN rather than once is that the nine runs within a cell took 285, 285, 285... to the second, with no warm-up effect -- each run builds a fresh LM, so dynamo's guards miss and inductor re-lowers the graph, and the on-disk cache does not rescue a fresh module instance. The controlled 2.0-2.5x benchmark was not wrong, it measured the steady-state step, which a 300-step run barely reaches. Compile is now conditional on run length (compile_min_steps=600): short calibration runs go eager, full 1221-step runs stay compiled. Numerics are unaffected -- the earlier noise-floor test showed eager and compiled differ by less than run-to-run non-determinism -- so this is purely a throughput decision, now taken per run rather than globally. This also explains why session 1 ran ~2.4x slower than projected: the projection was built from steady-state timings and never modelled a per-run fixed cost.
revisions.R32_orthogonal_init_has_no_bfloat16_kern: Crashed the first real grid 9 minutes in. init_lsuv calls torch.nn.init.orthogonal_, which runs a QR factorisation, and the LAPACK/cuSOLVER routine behind it (geqrf) has no bfloat16 kernel on CPU or CUDA. Models are built with .to(DEVICE, DTYPE) with DTYPE=bfloat16, so the run died with NotImplementedError: 'geqrf_cuda' not implemented for 'BFloat16' the moment the calibration loop reached the first lsuv arm. Only lsuv was affected -- every other init uses elementwise ops bfloat16 supports -- which is why fp16_control and standard finished first and the failure appeared to come out of nowhere. It survived the CPU checks because those exercised the model in float32; the dtype, not the logic, was the variable. Fixed by computing the QR on an fp32 scratch tensor and copying back: columns stay orthonormal through the round-trip (max |QtQ - I| ~ 1e-3, bf16 rounding rather than a broken factorisation) and the resulting std matches the 1/sqrt(fan_in) target to five decimals. The algorithm is unchanged; only the dtype the factorisation runs in. Verified end-to-end on a bf16 model: all six init functions now run, and lsuv_calibrate completes with LSUV_DEGENERATE populated (24 rescale ops, is_noop False) -- the first time the R13/R20 degeneracy measurement has actually produced a value.
revisions.R31_console_tee_and_export_layer: Two publication artifacts existed only as console output or not at all. (a) The statistics cell prints every H1-H8 verdict -- supported or not, p, Cohen's d, CI, Holm-corrected -- to stdout and nowhere else, across a grid spanning 3-4 sessions; a disconnect or a runtime restart would erase the single most important artifact for the paper. stdout is now mirrored to logs/console_YYYYMMDD.log on Drive, which duplicates no logic: the statistics cell remains the one source of truth and we simply keep what it says. (b) Added Cell 16: a tidy results_all_runs.csv (the data-availability artifact -- no reviewer wants 2800 JSON files), analysis_summary.csv, draft figure captions, and a README describing every artifact. It reads the RUN STORE rather than in-memory state, so it can be re-run in a fresh session at any time without repeating a GPU-second. Note on the captions: several plot titles assert a conclusion (e.g. 'causally shapes final sparsity'); the drafted captions describe what is shown and leave the inference to the text.
revisions.R30_session_budget_removed: The 22 h soft cutoff inside a 24 h Colab Pro+ session was discarding ~2 h per session -- about 8 h, or 10% of the whole experiment -- to guard against a failure the checkpoint layer already handles. save_run writes to a temp path and os.replace()s it, which is atomic on POSIX, so a session terminated mid-write cannot leave a truncated or half-parsed record; the store is either the old file or the new one. The genuine cost of an abrupt kill is therefore the single run in flight: roughly two minutes at the small scales and about seven at dim1536, which have_run() re-runs on the next Run All. Spending two hours to avoid losing seven minutes is the wrong trade. session_budget_hours=None now means 'run until the platform stops us'; budget_exceeded() returns False and every clean-stop path simply never fires. Setting it back to a number restores the soft cutoff unchanged, and the projection lines report against 24 h when it is None.
revisions.R29_cost_model_is_affine_not_proportiona: R28 fixed WHAT was timed; this fixes HOW it was extrapolated. Even with a correct sec/step at one scale, pricing the rest in proportion to FLOPs assumes constant throughput, and throughput is not constant: measured MFU runs from ~4% at dim192 to ~18% at dim1536 because small models are overhead-bound. Measured fixed overhead is 59.8 ms/step -- 89% of the entire step at dim192, 17% at dim1536. The real dim1536/dim192 cost ratio is ~9x against a FLOP ratio of ~39x, so extrapolating from the smallest scale over-priced the ladder ~2.5x (202 h projected against 55-75 h measured). Preflight now times three scales in steady state and fits sec/step = a + b*FLOPs_per_token, where the intercept IS the fixed overhead, so both regimes are represented rather than only one. The same steady-state timer replaced the compile A/B's contaminated measurement, which had reported 1.06x; it now reports 1.29x at dim192, consistent with the 2.01x and 2.48x measured directly at dim512 and dim1024. Note for the paper: this overhead structure is measured evidence and belongs in the efficiency discussion, which is otherwise entirely theoretical.
revisions.R28_preflight_projection_measured_the_wr: The Phase 0 projection reported 6459 GPU-hours / 294 sessions for a grid that direct measurement puts at 73-87 hours / 4 sessions. Cause: sec_per_step was (total wall time of a 30-step run)/30, an interval that also contains model construction, torch.compile warm-up paid once, and -- dominating -- the evaluation machinery. eval_every is a FRACTION of run length, so a 30-step run probes every 2 steps: roughly 260 evaluation forwards bolted onto 30 training steps, all of which amortise away in a real 1221-step run. Measured 2.066 s/step where the true steady-state figure at that scale is 0.084. An error of this size does not merely mislead, it would have caused a perfectly feasible experiment to be abandoned. Replaced with a dedicated post-warm-up timing window containing no evaluation; the raw smoke figure is still reported alongside it for comparison. The same contamination explains why the preflight compile A/B showed only 1.08x where a controlled benchmark showed 2.03x, and why its loss delta was meaningless: both arms were sliding down the steep early descent from the uninitialised-embedding starting point.
revisions.R26_divergence_guard: A benchmark on random tokens produced final losses of 48-122 where the uniform-prediction baseline is log(50257)=10.83, rising monotonically with model size -- i.e. divergence, and worse at scale. That run used no warmup on unlearnable data so it does not predict the real corpus, but it exposed a genuine hole: THERE WAS NO DIVERGENCE CHECK ANYWHERE. plateau_ok asks whether the val trace stopped descending, and an exploded run has also stopped descending, so it passes; val_ppl=exp(min(val,20)) then caps the damage into a finite, innocent-looking number. Because every claim is a seed-paired comparison, a few silent divergences in one arm would make the paired test measure optimisation stability rather than the rho0 mechanism -- manufacturing a large, significant, spurious effect for H1/H2/H5. Diverged runs are now flagged, kept on disk (so have_run does not re-run them), excluded from RESULTS, and counted in this manifest. STILL OPEN, to be settled in Phase 0 on real data: lr_grid=[1e-3,2e-3,3e-3] is aggressive for a 352M ternary model, and if all three diverge at the top scales the calibration would silently select the least-bad explosion.
revisions.R24_max_seq_len_never_rebound: FATAL, and it would have stopped the grid on run #1. Cfg carries TWO placeholder fields, vocab_size=8192 and max_seq_len=256, both meant to be rebound once the real tokenizer is known. Cell 9 rebound only vocab_size. RUN_CFG['seq_len'] is 512, and LM.__init__ builds the RoPE cos/sin buffers from c.max_seq_len, so the tables covered 256 positions while every batch carried 512 -- the first forward pass of every run raised 'The size of tensor a (512) must match the size of tensor b (256)'. Not a bias, not a slowdown: nothing could train at all. The existing schema/geometry guard reported PASSED for all 28 configs because it only validated Cfg fields against one another and never against RUN_CFG -- the two halves were each self-consistent and mutually contradictory. Fixed by rebinding max_seq_len alongside vocab_size, plus an assert that every config satisfies max_seq_len >= RUN_CFG['seq_len']. Found by a standalone benchmark that instantiated the real model at the real sequence length on CPU; the notebook's own preflight would also have hit it, but only after the corpus download, and the failure would have looked like a model bug rather than a config-binding bug.
revisions.R23_compile_enablement: PRE-RUN, follows R22. GAMMA_SCALE['val'] was read inside BitLinear.forward as a PYTHON FLOAT; dynamo specialises on python scalar values, so the two arms that move gamma every step by design (tai_warmup, sparse_sched) would have recompiled once per step and run SLOWER than eager -- torch.compile was therefore unusable. The float is now mirrored into a persistent 0-dim device tensor mutated in place, so the graph survives a changing threshold. The float remains the source of truth for every guard and log; all 17 write sites (including the three ablation cells, which run their own training loops) go through set_gamma(), and assert_quant_state_clean() cross-checks float against mirror at every run boundary -- a future edit that bypasses set_gamma fails loudly instead of silently ternarising at a stale threshold. Quantiser output verified BITWISE identical across 36 (shape, gamma, recipe) combinations. While writing that test, the mirror check itself was found to use an absolute 1e-9 tolerance against an fp32 tensor, which would have falsely aborted every sparse_sched run (its target 1.6 is not exact in fp32); changed to relative 1e-6. torch.compile remains OFF by default: preflight now runs an eager-vs-compiled A/B at the smallest scale and reports measured speedup AND loss parity, so the flag is flipped on evidence, not on hope. Also added: fused AdamW (these models have many small parameters, so the optimizer step was launch-bound) and a kernel profile in preflight, so the NEXT optimisation is chosen from measurement rather than a model.
revisions.R22_throughput_pass: PRE-RUN performance revision, applied BEFORE any GPU result existed, so no hypothesis, arm, or wording was chosen with knowledge of an outcome. Nothing that affects optimisation dynamics was touched: batch_size, seq_len, token budget, LR schedule, seed list, method set and all pre-registered hypotheses are unchanged. Changes: (1) FAST_MODE trades BIT-level reproducibility for flash-attention + cudnn autotuning; seed-level comparability (same init, same data order per seed) is preserved, which is what every claim here actually rests on -- see reproducibility_class below; (2) chunked cross-entropy: algebraically identical, ~4x lower peak VRAM, removes the OOM risk that threatened the R19 large scales; (3) vectorised get_batch -- verified to draw BIT-IDENTICAL token windows, so pre-patch runs stay comparable; (4) lm-eval scored in padded batches instead of ~2400 batch-1 forwards, and on the first lmeval_max_seeds seeds of each cell (same seeds for every method, so the paired test is unaffected); (5) LR calibration runs lr_cal_steps instead of the full budget -- its only output is an argmin over 3 LRs; (6) wallclock_equal_h1 defaults off (secondary H1 reading, re-ran the whole confirmatory grid); (7) the preflight wall-clock projection used n_params() as its cost proxy, which excludes the dim x vocab head -- dominant at small scales -- inflating the projection by roughly an order of magnitude; replaced with a per-token FLOP model.
revisions.R0_cfg_dataclass: n_layers/n_heads/ffn_hidden were swallowed by an end-of-line comment and were never dataclass fields -> every Cfg(...) call raised TypeError. Fixed + schema/geometry asserts added.
revisions.R0c_gqa_kv_heads: n_kv_heads was n_heads//2, not a divisor for odd head counts (e.g. dim320: 5%2!=0), which would have malformed the whole decoder_v2 ladder behind H7. Now the largest proper divisor.
revisions.R1_dead_fixed_point: init_tai advertised an 8-step fixed-point search whose output was bit-identical with the loop removed (vals recomputed each iteration; dormant mass always below threshold; final std-norm makes am/dm scale irrelevant). Replaced by the closed-form construction + explicit realised-rho0 verification.
revisions.R2_tai_hyperparams: dm/jitter were hard-coded magic numbers with no sensitivity analysis. Now explicit (TAI_HP), swept in Cell 13c-b, and the separation bound is asserted rather than assumed.
revisions.R3_plateau_gate: the gate compared mean(tail) to final on the SINGLE-BATCH TRAIN loss: dominated by batch noise (perfectly flat traces passed only 63-100% of the time depending on sigma), and a level test that cosine LR decay satisfies mechanically. Replaced by a slope test with CI on the held-out VAL trace, rejecting both still-descending and ascending tails.
revisions.R5_h4_data_variance: H4 was measured at one val fold; the old cell called this unfixable without persisting weights. The model is in memory at the end of train_run, so all K folds are now scored there (val_loss_folds) and H4's Levene runs on pooled seed x fold.
revisions.R6_mechanism_control: TAI was the only arm able to move rho0 at all, making H3 nearly unfalsifiable. gamma_offset reaches the same rho0 via a constant threshold scale c=gamma_scale_for_rho0(rho0) with a STANDARD init, giving a mechanism-matched competitor for H3/H5.
revisions.R13_lsuv_not_lsuv: init_lsuv was orthogonal-init + a static rescale, not LSUV. The grid sold {standard,lsuv} as two locked-rho0 FAMILIES (measured: 0.6900 vs 0.6906 -- one family) and took the per-seed BEST of them as a baseline, i.e. max-selection over one family. Implementing LSUV properly showed it is DEGENERATE here: BitLinear pre-normalises, so output variance at init is 1.0004 and calibration rescales nothing. Measured (LSUV_DEGENERATE), reported, and the H7 baseline rebuilt on bitnet158 + gamma_offset.
revisions.R19_extended_scaling_ladder: the original ladder topped out at 117M non-embed params, so H6's scaling claim spanned <1 order of magnitude on an n=9 slope. Added dim1280 (214M), dim1536 (352M) as EXPLORATORY points and dim2048 (783M) as opt-in, extending the confirmatory-to-largest span past 1.5 orders of magnitude (2.16, or 2.50 with the opt-in point). At a single-A100 budget these cannot be trained compute-optimally, so they are token-equal and their role is H6 SIGN-consistency, not an absolute-loss comparison -- stated explicitly rather than presented as convergence. Verified: 352M model builds, forwards, and takes a correct TAI init (realised rho0=0.7504) on CPU. Also fixed the wall-clock projection (counted every declared config, incl. the opt-in 783M, inflating the estimate) and a TARGET_LOSS print KeyError on unrun scales.
revisions.R18_undefined_vars_crashed_stats: cell 18 -- the PRIMARY statistics cell computing H1-H4 -- referenced two names that were never defined: `cp` (in the per-method summary dict) and `cpm` (in the summary print). Both were remnants of a 'copy accuracy' metric that was never implemented. Either one raises NameError on the FIRST method of the FIRST scale, so the entire confirmatory analysis produced nothing -- H1, H2, H3, H4 all crashed before printing. Found by executing the cell on synthetic RESULTS; removed both. This bug was invisible to every static read because the names looked like plausible locals.
revisions.R17_placebo_inverted: train_run routed init by method.startswith('tai'), which also matches 'tai_negctrl' -- so H3's PRE-REGISTERED FALSIFICATION arm silently received the real, rho0-honouring TAI init, and apply_init's tai_negctrl branch was unreachable dead code. The placebo therefore tracked rho0 as strongly as the true arm (Spearman ~+1) against a frozen prediction of 'FLAT (~0)', and Cell 15 would have reported that under h3_strong_falsification: the paper's most rigorous instrument would have concluded the primary contribution is an artefact even if the real effect were sound. A broken placebo does not weaken a claim, it inverts it. Routing is now explicit and order-independent, with a per-run assertion that the placebo's realised rho0 stays at 0.69 regardless of label (verified: flat 30.9% across labels 0.4-0.9 while the real arm moves 59.7% -> 9.8%).
revisions.R15_holdout_leak: the split promised 'K interleaved val folds' but built K CONTIGUOUS slices, and derived TRAIN per fold while only fold 0's TRAIN was ever trained on. R5 then scored folds 1..K-1 -- which sit INSIDE that TRAIN (measured: 100% overlap). H4's 'data-sampling variance' would have been four train-loss readings mislabelled as held-out. Rebuilt: ONE genuinely interleaved held-out region (every stride-th chunk across the corpus), removed from training once, then split into K unseen sub-folds sharing a single TRAIN.
revisions.R16_sparsity_measured_wrong: BitLinear.sparsity() hard-coded gamma_scale=1 and ignored QUANT_MODE/GAMMA_SCALE, so it reported a counterfactual rather than the forward pass that ran. gamma_offset (whose entire mechanism IS a shifted gamma) measured ~31% at every rho0 -- flat -- which would have made H3's mechanism control, H5's second frontier and fig10 'prove' that gamma_offset cannot control sparsity when only the ruler was wrong (smoke-run: 31.0% before vs 25.1% after, matching TAI's 24.9%). It also reported 31.2% for fp16_control, which quantises nothing, and could never return 0 -- silently disarming R14's leak guard. Now mirrors forward exactly; the canonical-threshold reading survives as sparsity_at_default_gamma() for Cell 13b.
revisions.R14_global_state_leak: train_run set QUANT_MODE/QUANT_RECIPE globally and restored them ~64 lines later with no try/finally. SystemExit at the session boundary is this notebook's DESIGNED control flow, so an fp16_control run hitting the budget leaked full_precision=True into the next session: later 'tai'/'bitnet158' runs would train in FULL PRECISION, look plausible, save under a valid run_id, and be skipped forever by have_run(). Fixed with a quant_state context manager (restores on every exit path), an entry assertion (fails loudly on a dirty state), and a post-hoc guard rejecting any ternary run reporting final_sparsity==0. Same leak closed in cells 22/24/25.
revisions.R7_efficiency_framing: the measured table was presented as 'efficiency'; with STE it measures the cost of SIMULATING ternary in bf16 and is expected to be slower than fp16. Reframed: theoretical deployment model is primary, simulation cost is secondary and labelled.

h2_claim_as_stated: quality at a fixed 20M-token budget (convergence NOT established)
h3_operative_wording: rho0 leaves a small, perfectly ordered, highly reproducible RESIDUAL on final sparsity; the large majority of the initial intervention is erased by training, which pulls every operating point back toward an attractor near the value the `standard` arm reaches unaided. H3 is NOT supported in its strong pre-registered form and must be reported as a bounded residual effect with the retention fraction stated.
h6_operative_wording: direction consistent across scales; magnitude NOT resolved as scale-varying (primary scale-level CI spans zero; seed-clustered intervals are anticonservative for a scale-level question -- see R43)

h2_prereg_status: UNTESTABLE: the pre-registered H2 is an equivalence claim about CONVERGED quality over plateau-verified paired seeds, and no run reached plateau at the 20M-token budget (0/760; independently confirmed by the 2x-budget check in budget_sufficiency). Reported as unresolved, NOT as a null result. See h2_token_equal_companion for the weaker, testable claim and R45 for why the companion is not a post-hoc substitution.

h3_retention.interpretation: fraction of the initial operating-point intervention that survives training; ~1.0 would mean rho0 sets final sparsity, ~0.0 means training erases it entirely

h2_operative_wording: at a fixed 20M-token budget (NOT converged; the val trace is still descending at budget end, so no claim may say 'converged quality')
divergence_rule: val_loss > 1.25*log(vocab) (=13.53), non-finite, or a late 1.5x rise in the val trace. A model that learned NOTHING still scores log(vocab); above that is divergence, not poor training.
reproducibility_class: statistical (seed-level): identical init + data order per seed; bit-level rerun equality NOT guaranteed
baseline_family_note: standard and lsuv are ONE family in this architecture (rho0 0.6900 vs 0.6906; LSUV degenerate under RMSNorm pre-normalisation). The genuine second family is gamma_offset, which differs at the operating point.
efficiency_limitation: no ternary kernel benchmarked; deployment numbers are an arithmetic model, measured numbers are simulation overhead
stats_dependency_note: All confirmatory tests (paired t, Wilcoxon, bootstrap CI, Holm, TOST equivalence, Levene) use scipy only and run without statsmodels; statsmodels is used ONLY for the secondary H6 mixed-effects slope, which falls back to a descriptive per-scale OLS if statsmodels is absent. No confirmatory claim depends on an optional package.
validity_banner: Real FineWeb-EDU (GPT-2 BPE) corpus used; lm-eval scored.
